units.function: Pure helper tests for normalized Agent display-name collision detection and automatic numeric suffix selection.
units.dependencyDirection: AgentService passes an in-memory Agent name/status set to shortname normalization helpers before create/update naming; no database constraint or external dependency is involved.
units.keyDataModels: Agent id/name/status, normalized shortname, excluded Agent id and generated numeric suffix.
units.lifecycle: Active Agents collide after normalization, the Agent being updated is excluded, names with no normalized shortname do not collide and terminated Agents are ignored. Deduplication retains the original name or appends/increments a suffix until the snapshot appears unique.
units.testAssessment: Eight small cases cover normalization, termination, self-exclusion, empty normalized names and suffix progression. Missing are Company scoping, Unicode/confusables/case locale, reserved names, very long values, database uniqueness, concurrent creates, deleted/reactivated Agents, historical reference ambiguity and deterministic behavior under duplicate existing names.
units.designRationale: Keep UI-friendly Agent handles readable and avoid common naming clashes while allowing names from retired Agents to be reused.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs stable human-readable labels without ever using them as identity, authorization or responsibility references, and must preserve clarity across termination/reactivation and imports.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Use immutable opaque Agent/Principal ids and separately scoped, database-constrained slugs with Unicode-confusable policy and optimistic retry. Treat display names as non-unique. Do not automatically reuse a terminated Agent's slug where historical responsibility views could become ambiguous; require an explicit alias lifecycle.
units.responsibilityConflict: Reusing a normalized shortname after termination can make audit exports and human approvals appear to refer to a new Agent when older records used the same label. Snapshot-only suffixing races under concurrent creation and provides no proof of identity continuity.

units.function: Schema compatibility tests for optional provenance/display metadata on Agent Skill entries and legacy snapshots that omit those fields.
units.dependencyDirection: Shared Zod validators parse Adapter-produced Skill entries/snapshots before server routes and Web projections consume them; provenance is descriptive and optional.
units.keyDataModels: Skill key/runtime name, desired/managed/state, Adapter type/mode, origin/origin label/location label/readOnly/detail and warnings.
units.lifecycle: New entries may describe a user-installed external read-only Skill and its filesystem location, while older snapshots without any provenance continue to parse unchanged.
units.testAssessment: Two narrow schema cases prove optional-field acceptance and backward compatibility. Missing are allowed origin/state transitions, package/version/digest/license/signature, publisher, install time, trust and review status, permission/tool/data manifest, location sanitization, tamper detection, legacy quarantine and whether readOnly is enforced rather than displayed.
units.designRationale: Improve Skill UI transparency without breaking existing Adapter snapshots or forcing all runtimes to provide provenance immediately.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a verifiable Skill/Plugin supply-chain contract that distinguishes desired configuration from installed code and prevents unreviewed instructions/tools from gaining enterprise authority.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the separation of desired/managed/runtime state and provenance presentation, but make PackageVersion provenance mandatory for newly admitted Skills: source, immutable digest, license, publisher/signature, compatibility, permissions/data egress and review status. Legacy entries without provenance must be visibly unverified and blocked from production activation until admitted, not silently accepted as equivalent.
units.responsibilityConflict: Optional labels and a readOnly boolean are not evidence of origin or integrity. A legacy Skill can remain active with no accountable installer, review, digest or authority manifest, undermining responsibility and data-governance claims.

units.function: Route tests for running Adapter environment diagnostics on the explicitly selected sandbox/remote target, managing test leases and merging Environment Secret/plain variables with Agent config.
units.dependencyDirection: The route authorizes Company Adapter configuration, resolves Environment and Secret bindings, acquires/realizes a fresh execution lease, resolves an Adapter execution target, invokes Adapter.testEnvironment with merged config and always releases the driver lease with released/failed status.
units.keyDataModels: Company Environment/driver/config/envVars, SecretRef/missing binding, execution lease/workspace/target, Adapter config env, diagnostic check/status and sandbox/provider/snapshot identity detail.
units.lifecycle: Missing or unsupported requested environments return structured diagnostics without host probing. A supported target uses a fresh non-reused lease with custom image, archives it on release and reports sandbox identity. Workspace failure marks/releases the lease failed. Environment env is the base layer, Agent env wins, protected PAPERCLIP_API_KEY is filtered, and missing Secret bindings add failure checks; however the Adapter probe still runs with remaining variables when a binding is missing.
units.testAssessment: Seven route cases cover the critical no-host-fallback invariant, missing target, happy-path lease identity/release, realization failure, env precedence/protected key filtering and missing-binding diagnostics. Missing are real authorization denials, cross-Company environment id, probe timeout/cancel/network policy, malicious Adapter output, lease cleanup failure, archive retention/privacy, Secret redaction in diagnostic/error/logs, Agent override of protected environment policy, idempotency/rate limits and a fail-before-execute assertion for missing required Secrets.
units.designRationale: Make configuration tests reflect the environment where work will actually run, keep failed sandboxes inspectable and prevent misleading success from probing the control-plane host instead of an unsupported remote target.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a safe Connector/Environment certification probe that never escapes to the host, never runs with an incomplete authority set and produces a structured, attributable health attestation for managed-cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT explicit-target/no-host-fallback, fresh lease, structured diagnostics, protected control-plane keys and release-on-all-paths. Resolve and validate all required Secret/data bindings before executing any probe; apply an allowlisted env merge where policy-owned keys cannot be overridden by Agent config. Run probes in an isolated, egress-limited disposable sandbox and return a signed short-lived HealthAttestation. Archive only after explicit diagnostic-retention policy and Secret scrubbing.
units.responsibilityConflict: A missing required Secret still permits partial probe execution, which can create effects under a different authority set than the approved runtime. Agent config wins env conflicts without shown policy classification. The test action has no accountable requester/approval/audit receipt, and archived failed sandboxes may retain enterprise data or credentials.
